target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying evals and RL environments; also businesses licensing codebases or operating data
problem: Labs need realistic environments and evals built from real production work to measure and train models.
business_model: Sells RL environments and datasets to labs; sources data from licensing businesses' codebases and de-identified operating data

founders.name: Nalu Concepcion
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; roles were software engineer, product manager, data scientist.

founders.name: Tony Goss
founders.background_notes: YC page says he hacked Dark Forest to win $400k.

competitors.name: Mercor, Surge, Handshake, Turing
competitors.what: Human data vendors adding RL environments
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as moving into environments

technical_complexity.rationale: Digital twins of real businesses and thousands of coding evals demand strong engineering, but not research-grade novelty.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed real-world operating data is a modest edge; labs can build in-house and vendors are large.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Vendors entered RL environments in 2025; no action against idler found.

market_need_then: Demand from labs for RL environments surged in 2025; idler says it built thousands of coding evals for an unnamed lab in its first year.

identity.logo: Logo shown on site; not described further
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident research lab tone ('Push the frontier of your model')

branding.community_and_virality: Launch covered by deal news sites in August 2026; founders known from the Dark Forest community.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive name but 'idler' implies inactivity; little brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Active as of 2026-11. Reported $9M Paradigm-led seed and a public benchmark, plus a founding team with game-hacking and crypto lab backgrounds, suggest strong early momentum; the risks are lab in-housing and large data vendors.
notes: The $9M seed is reported by Runtimewire (paywalled teaser, published 2026-08-19), Dealroom news and raising.fi; the company site does not mention funding and rl-list says the company has not confirmed it. A Cornell bulletin dated 2025-12-16 reportedly mentions the seed, so closing may predate the announcement; date used is the announcement. The investor list (YC, Long Journey) comes from a search summary of The SaaS News. Another listing shows $500K and Series A, which conflicts.
